results.title: Hopes of shedding light on healthcare impact
results.description: A new collaboration between Sjúkratryggingar Íslands [Icelandic Health Insurance] and the Danish company Frameshift aims to use Icelandic data and compare them with Danish healthcare databases. The collaboration is intended to strengthen analytical capacity, support decision-making and provide a better overview of costs and outcomes in the healthcare system. Sigurður H. Helgason, CEO of Sjúkratryggingar Íslands, says there is a large amount of data in healthcare which could be used more extensively to improve decision-making. For example, it could be used to examine, in a broad sense, what impact healthcare services have on people's lives. This dataset that the Danes have created gives us an opportunity to look not only at healthcare and what healthcare consists of, but also at how diseases affect people's lives. It would also be possible to examine how assistance from healthcare services can help offset the negative effects of disease. He says the collaboration could lead to better use of funding and provide insight into which interventions have the most positive effects. The collaboration will initially focus on specific projects. The first will focus on endometriosis. Sigurður points out that the condition is often regarded as a hidden problem which has not been adequately addressed. It can also have a significant negative impact on everyday life and participation in the labour market. That is why this is a good example to examine. To examine the relationship between living with this condition, receiving particular services and what effect that has on key variables in patients' lives - such as employment income, participation in the labour market and so on. Sigurður explains that the link with the Danish dataset offers the opportunity to connect healthcare data with a wide range of data describing people's circumstances. It is exciting for us to explore that.

results.title: Rise in US preteen suicide rate alarms mental health experts
results.description: Since 2008, rate of preteen suicide has increased by an average of 8.2% annually.
